issues.label: Reasonable suspicion for initial stop
issues.why: Court must determine whether the observed jaywalking gave police reasonable suspicion to justify an investigatory stop.

issues.label: Whether encounter was consensual or Terry stop
issues.why: The nature of the police-citizen encounter determines what constitutional justification was required before K.J. fled.

issues.label: Flight from police as probable cause
issues.why: Court characterized running as creating probable cause for obstruction, and must correctly apply Ohio law on flight.

issues.label: Whether flight alone constitutes obstructing official business
issues.why: Ohio law questions whether merely fleeing, without an affirmative act, satisfies the obstruction statute.

issues.label: Probable cause to arrest for obstruction
issues.why: Court relied on obstruction probable cause to validate the arrest and ensuing search.

issues.label: Validity of jaywalking predicate for stop
issues.why: CMC 506.46 elements and whether crossing without a crosswalk was actually unlawful underpin the stop's legality.

issues.label: Legality of apartment search
issues.why: The gun was found in an apartment K.J. entered; the search's constitutional basis (consent, warrant, exigency) must be assessed.

issues.label: Standing to challenge apartment search
issues.why: K.J.'s expectation of privacy in an apartment he fled into affects his ability to suppress the gun.

issues.label: Attenuation and fruit of poisonous tree
issues.why: If the stop was unlawful, whether the gun and statements were sufficiently attenuated must be evaluated.

issues.label: Sufficiency: carrying concealed weapon
issues.why: Evidence must show K.J. knowingly carried a concealed operable firearm on his person.

issues.label: Concealment element proof
issues.why: No officer saw the gun on K.J.'s person or in the bag, raising concealment sufficiency concerns.

issues.label: Sufficiency: tampering with evidence
issues.why: Requires proof K.J. knew of an investigation and altered/concealed evidence to impair its availability.

issues.label: Overlap of concealment and tampering
issues.why: Whether hiding the gun supports both concealed-carry and tampering, or constitutes allied offenses.

issues.label: Firearm operability proof
issues.why: Operability is an element for the weapons charge, addressed by test-firing testimony.

issues.label: Possession/nexus of firearm to K.J.
issues.why: Court must find sufficient evidence linking K.J. to the gun found hidden in the closet.

issues.label: Sufficiency: obstructing official business
issues.why: Requires an affirmative act done with purpose to prevent a lawful official function.

issues.label: Whether officers performed lawful duty
issues.why: Obstruction requires the officer to be engaged in a lawful, authorized act at the time.

issues.label: Manifest weight: jaywalking adjudication
issues.why: K.J. argues the traffic-offender finding is against the manifest weight of evidence.

issues.label: Address discrepancies in citations/reports
issues.why: Inconsistent offense addresses may affect credibility and proof of the jaywalking violation.

issues.label: Effect of dismissed and refiled citation
issues.why: The jaywalking citation's dismissal and refiling raises procedural and speedy-trial-type questions.

issues.label: Reliability of collective knowledge/radio relay
issues.why: Stop justification rested on relayed observations, invoking the collective-knowledge doctrine.

issues.label: High-crime area as factor
issues.why: Court must weigh, without overweighting, the neighborhood characterization in the reasonable-suspicion analysis.

issues.label: Admissibility of K.J.'s custodial statements
issues.why: K.J.'s admissions to Officer Clark require Miranda and voluntariness scrutiny for juveniles.

issues.label: Juvenile-specific interrogation safeguards
issues.why: K.J.'s age and juvenile status affect the voluntariness and waiver analysis of his statements.

issues.label: Allied offenses/merger at disposition
issues.why: Whether the weapons and tampering offenses should merge for sentencing must be considered.

issues.label: Standard of review for suppression
issues.why: Court must apply proper mixed factual-deference and de novo legal review on appeal.

issues.label: Standard of review sufficiency vs manifest weight
issues.why: Different standards govern the sufficiency and manifest-weight challenges raised.
